extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners) on (1) when amendments should or should not be entered into the record and procedural handling of such papers, and (2) the standards for using affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 to antedate/rebut prior art references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the question of new matter is settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice of nonentry because of alleged new matter does not apply to amendments to the specification and claims. See MPEP § 714.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks (37 CFR 1.3) submitted to TC Director
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the opinion of the examiner, brings it within the condemnation of 37 CFR 1.3, will be submitted to the Technology Center (TC) Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the TC Director determines the remarks violate 37 CFR 1.3, he or she will notify the applicant of the non-entry of the paper. See MPEP § 714.25 and § 1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink (easily erasable paper) are not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments on so-called 'easily erasable paper' (i.e., not in permanent ink) should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.07 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment presenting claims in excess of number paid without fee is not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee or authorization to charge the fee will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509 and § 607 for fees and payment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment canceling all claims to elected invention and presenting only nonelected claims is nonresponsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered; it is nonresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP § 714.03 and § 714.05. See MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment not complying with 37 CFR 1.121 is not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment including changes to the specification/claims which is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., one which does not include replacement paragraphs or claim listings) should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714 for compliance details and required formatting (replacement paragraphs, claim listings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with preparation of first Office action may be denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with the preparation of a first Office action may be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for denying entry of a preliminary amendment are set forth in 37 CFR 1.115(b). See MPEP § 714.01(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply not entered as matter of right unless filed during suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply is not entered as a matter of right unless it is filed during a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2) and MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments may later be entered after applicant's subsequent showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments falling within non-entry categories should not be entered at filing time, but a subsequent showing by applicant may lead to entry of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider applicant submissions that cure the non-entry issue and enter the amendment if an adequate showing is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: amendments should not be entered in part
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid confusion of the record the general rule prevails that an amendment should not be entered in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict observance may sometimes work more harm than infraction would; exceptions exist (see following exception entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: substitute specification with amendments may be entered in part (deny entry of substitute spec)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'amendment' presenting an unacceptable substitute specification along with amendatory matter (e.g., amendments to claims or new claims) should be entered in part: the substitute specification should be denied entry and so marked, while the rest of the paper should be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be advised that the substitute specification has not been entered. See 37 CFR 1.125 and MPEP § 608.01(q). Under current practice, proper substitute specifications may be voluntarily filed and will normally be accepted; however, entry after a notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.312) is not a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: 37 CFR 1.312 amendment entered only as to approved part
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 which in part is approved and in other part disapproved is entered only as to the approved part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: after prosecution closed (Ex Parte Quayle), amendment entered only as to formal matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application where prosecution on the merits is closed (after issuance of an Ex Parte Quayle action), an amendment curing a noted formal defect and adding claims that the examiner considers unpatentable or requiring further search will be entered only as to the formal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has no right to have new claims considered or entered at this point in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part entered only to extent granted
rubrics_metrics.description: In an amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part, the amendment is entered only to the extent that the motion was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner marks 'Enter' in red ink opposite enterable portions; follow IFW Manual for electronic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertently entered amendments have no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect, and the same action is taken as if the changes had not been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless unauthorized entry is deleted, note the margin of the amendatory paper 'Not Officially Entered.' If retained in file even though not entered, give a paper number and list on file wrapper with notation 'Not Entered.' See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourtesy of Applicant or Attorney — comply with 37 CFR 1.3
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy; papers violating this may be submitted to the Director and not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff should briefly review all papers before entry to determine discourteous remarks. If discourteous, the remarks may be ignored or the paper submitted to the TC Director for review (see MPEP § 1003). Complaints against examiners/employees must be made in separate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration may be submitted to establish invention of the subject matter of the rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference or activity on which the rejection is based; used to 'swear back' the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date of references defined (publication dates, effective filing dates). Prior invention may not be established for activities in countries before specified NAFTA/WTO effective dates. The showing must be of such character and weight to establish reduction to practice or conception plus due diligence; original exhibits or satisfactorily explained absence required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of 37 CFR 1.131 — antedating references under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations may be used to antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), e.g., where the prior art date is less than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date (subject to 'same patentable invention' limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art reference under 102(a) is a U.S. patent or application publication, the reference may not be antedated if it claims the same patentable invention. See MPEP § 715.05 for 'same patentable invention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of 37 CFR 1.131 — antedating references under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations may be used to antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) where the reference has a prior art date prior to applicant's effective filing date and shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for 'same patentable invention' discussion and MPEP §§ 706.02(a), 2136–2136.03 for which references qualify under 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 if reference is more than 1 year prior (statutory bar 35 U.S.C. 102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate when the reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date (a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References that only qualify under 102(a) or (e) are not statutory bars; check filing/publication dates carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 if reference claims the same patentable invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claims the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 and MPEP Chapter 2300. If reference and application are commonly owned and not patentably distinct, consider terminal disclaimer or 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit to overcome 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection (MPEP § 718).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 for certain foreign patents (35 U.S.C. 102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is inappropriate where the reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant or patent owner issued prior to the filing date of the domestic application if the foreign application was filed more than 12 months prior to the domestic filing (35 U.S.C. 102(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check foreign filing dates and domestic priority rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 when earlier effective filing date exists (parent application or international convention date)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 is unnecessary where the effective filing date of applicant's parent application or an international convention proved filing date is prior to the effective date of the reference; the reference should not have been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 201.11–201.15 regarding priority and effective filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 where double patenting applies
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference is a prior U.S. patent to the same entity claiming the same invention (double patenting issue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider double patenting doctrine and appropriate remedies (terminal disclaimer, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 where doctrine of dedication applies
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference is the disclosure of a prior U.S. patent to the same party, not copending (dedication to the public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Gibbs and subsequent case law; check whether dedication doctrine applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 where applicant has clearly admitted subject matter is prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where applicant has clearly admitted on the record that subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions cannot be overcome by 1.131 affidavits. See cited cases (Hellsund, Garfinkel, Blout, Lopresti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 for subject matter available under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used to overcome references where the subject matter relied upon is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate procedural mechanism for 102(f) issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 for subject matter available under 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used to overcome references where the subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 102(g) indicates the subject matter was made before applicant's invention; 1.131 is designed for rebutting mere presumption of prior creation (102(a)/(e)), not actual prior invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use of 37 CFR 1.131 for lost counts in interferences that are 102(g) or estopped
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used where the subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) or barred to applicant by interference estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cases (Bandel, Kroekel, Deckler) and exceptions (Zletz) where a showing that the now claimed invention is not 'substantially the same' may permit 1.131 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date to be overcome is the effective date of the reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131 is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine effective date according to reference type (see next entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and WIPO publications
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and WIPO publications of international applications are available as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e); the effective date to be overcome is their effective filing/publication date determined under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 706.02(a), 706.02(f)(1), 2136–2136.03 for detailed discussions. The effective date of a domestic patent used as a reference is not the foreign filing date to which the application may have been entitled under 35 U.S.C. 119(a) (In re Hilmer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: See MPEP §§ 2126–2127 regarding the date of availability of foreign patents as prior art; determine effective date per those rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patent availability rules can differ; consult cited MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed publication, including a published foreign patent application, is effective as of its publication date, not its date of receipt by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2128–2128.02 for additional information on effective dates of printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For activities (e.g., public use, on-sale, knowledge by others), the effective date of the activity used to reject the claims is the date the activity was first known to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may have made an admission or submitted evidence; examiners may have personal knowledge. See MPEP §§ 706.02(c) and 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.57 — Affidavit/Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131: Ineffective - Heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to state: 'The [1] filed on [2] under 37 CFR 1.131 has been considered but is ineffective to overcome the [3] reference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be followed by one or more of form paragraphs 7.58–7.63 or a paragraph setting forth the proper basis for insufficiency (e.g., failure to establish acts performed in this country, scope not commensurate with claim). Examiner notes indicate bracket insertions and sequencing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.59 — Ineffective: Insufficient evidence of reduction to practice before reference date
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to explain that evidence submitted is insufficient to establish a reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA/WTO member country prior to the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.57; bracket 2 must explain the lack of showing. Use when reduction to practice is at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.60 — Ineffective: Reference is a statutory bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that the reference is a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and thus cannot be overcome by a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.61 — Ineffective: Insufficient evidence of conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that the evidence submitted is insufficient to establish conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference, including that conception must be more than a vague idea and capable of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.57 and include explanation of deficiency in bracket 2. If affidavit also fails to establish diligence or reduction to practice, follow with 7.62/7.63 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.58 — Ineffective: Claiming same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that the reference is a U.S. patent or application publication that claims the rejected invention, making 37 CFR 1.131 inappropriate when the reference claims the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.57 and include explanation of deficiency. If affidavit improperly filed under 1.131 but is actually a 1.132 matter, it will be considered as though filed under 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.62 — Ineffective: Diligence lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that evidence is insufficient to establish diligence from a date prior to the date of reduction to practice of the reference to either constructive or actual reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57; explain reasons for non-diligence in bracket 2; follow-up sequencing rules with 7.61 or 7.63 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.63 — Ineffective: Insufficient evidence of actual reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that evidence is insufficient to establish alleged actual reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA/WTO member country after the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57; do not use if alleged reduction to practice is prior to the effective date of the reference (use 7.59). Explain lack of showing in bracket 2; sequence with 7.61/7.62 if those also fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.64 — Affidavit/Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131: Effective to overcome reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to state that the affidavit or declaration filed under 37 CFR 1.131 is sufficient to overcome the identified reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert affidavit/declaration type and filing date in brackets; follow examiner notes for bracket content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 versus 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations are for overcoming a prior art rejection by proving invention prior to the effective date of the reference or activity; 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits/declarations (or an affidavit under 1.132 considered as such if improperly filed under 1.131) are used to establish that the subject matter relied on in the reference/publication was the invention of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, file the correct type. Affidavits improperly filed under 1.131 but intended to show the reference is applicant's invention will be considered under 1.132 (In re Facius). Use 1.132 when the reference is a publication of applicant's own invention or to show derivation/ownership issues (see MPEP § 716.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint patent/publication to applicant and another — use 1.131 or 1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a jointly filed patent/application publication by applicant and another is later claimed by applicant, the joint patent/publication is a valid reference unless overcome by 1.131 or an unequivocal 1.132 declaration by applicant that he/she conceived the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re DeBaun and MPEP § 716.10 for use of 1.132 to overcome such rejections; a disclaimer by the co-patentee need not be required but may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common assignee does not avoid necessity of filing 1.131/1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: Common ownership of the reference and the later application does not, by itself, avoid the necessity of filing an affidavit or declaration under 1.131 unless a showing under 1.132 that the patentee derived the subject matter from the applicant is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rejections are applied under 102(f)/103 or 102(g)/103 (or 102(e)/103 for post-Nov 29, 1999 filings), a showing that the invention was commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time of the later invention may preclude or overcome such a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference is publication of applicant's own invention — 1.131/1.132 implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the reference is a statutory bar, a rejection based on a publication may be overcome by showing it was published by applicant or on applicant's behalf; such a showing is not made to prove a date of invention under 1.131, so NAFTA/WTO country date restrictions do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cases (Lemieux, Powell) and MPEP § 716.10 regarding 1.132 affidavits to show a reference is applicant's own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authorship — applicant as co-author may antedate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant is one of the co-authors of a publication cited against his/her application, the applicant may overcome the rejection by filing a 1.131 affidavit/declaration or a specific 1.132 affidavit/declaration establishing the article described applicant's own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit by applicant alone indicating applicant is sole inventor and others were working under his/her direction can remove the publication as a 102(a) reference. See In re Katz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation — evidence that patentee derived subject matter from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: When unclaimed subject matter of a patent or publication is applicant's own invention, a rejection (not a statutory bar) may be removed by submitting evidence establishing that the patentee/author derived the knowledge from applicant and that applicant made the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Mathews and In re Facius for derivation proof standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities applied against the claims can be antedated by 1.131 (if not statutory bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is a statutory bar, a rejection based on an activity showing the claimed invention was used or known prior to filing may be overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 establishing a date of invention prior to the activity; alternatively, a 1.132 affidavit may show the activity was performed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.02 and 715.01(d) for specifics; proper evidentiary showing required.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much of the claimed invention must be shown in a 1.131 affidavit — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), so the claim as a whole reads on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Tanczyn: showing part of a multi-element claim that omits an element may be insufficient. However, if examiner has treated a claim limitation as obvious (in a 103 rejection) and has not cited a reference teaching that limitation, a 1.131 affidavit may be sufficient even if it does not show that particular feature or modification (In re Stryker). Also, an affidavit need not show identical disclosure of the reference if it shows completion commensurate with the extent of the invention claimed (In re Wakefield).
